taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America. Keep distinct from Croton fruticosus.
look_here_first: Start with growth form and leaf margin: this is a woody/subshrubby Croton, with ovate to ovate-lanceolate leaves and fine serrulation rather than an entire margin.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis is voucher-backed by the UT Plant Resources Center. Comal is locked by preserved ILLS specimen ILLS00139680 near Canyon Lake. Kerr is locked by Heller's 1894 southern-Texas exploration documenting C. fruticulosus on both banks of the Guadalupe at Kerrville.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Use exact county voucher or field documentation; do not infer local counties from broad Edwards Plateau or southwestern Texas range statements.

best_field_traits: petioles short relative to the leaf blade
bisexual racemes typically several centimeters long
three styles bifid to six terminal segments
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Croton lindheimeri is an annual herb with mostly entire leaves. Croton texensis is annual and strictly dioecious, with narrower mostly entire leaves and unisexual inflorescences.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Woody/subshrubby habit plus serrulate leaves separate C. fruticulosus from the more herbaceous, mostly entire-leaved local Crotons.
